title: X-linked recessive carriers
goal: A reader can trace three generations of X-linked recessive inheritance, distinguish affected males and carrier females from unaffected relatives, and identify the proband and each child's parents.

rubric.must: Three distinct generation rows have readable Roman-numeral labels I, II, and III, and every individual has a readable generation-and-number identifier beside the correct symbol.
II-1 and III-3 are fully filled squares; I-2, II-4, and III-2 are circles with distinct central carrier dots; all other individuals have empty symbols, with every symbol outline recognizable.
The descent lines show affected II-1 as a child of I-1 and carrier I-2, and affected III-3 as a child of II-3 and carrier II-4.
Affected father II-1 and unaffected mother II-2 visibly have an unaffected son III-1 and a carrier daughter III-2, with no affected son connected to their union.
Unaffected II-5 is visibly a child of the generation-I couple and forms a separate union with unaffected II-6, from which unaffected III-5 descends.
Exactly one family member has a proband arrow labeled P, and its tip identifies III-3 without touching another person's symbol or a descent line.
Each generation-III descent line can be followed to exactly one parental union without passing through an unrelated person's symbol, identifier, carrier dot, or proband marker.

ideal.notes: Carrier females carry a central dot and affected males are solid squares across three generations; affected father II-1 has an unaffected son and a carrier daughter, and proband III-3 descends from carrier mother II-4.
